sections.title: The letter e
paragraphs: The letter name is (e) /ə/. Its main sound is a vowel, which is a sound made with open air. You hear it in the word (menu) /mə.ny/, which means a list of dishes. This letter has four different sounds across French words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, keep your tongue in the centre of your mouth. Push your lips forward into a small circle. For the second sound, pull your lips wide and raise your tongue near your upper teeth. For the third sound, keep your lips wide and drop your jaw slightly lower. Place two fingers on your cheeks to feel your lips round or spread.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In short words like (le) /lə/, or inside an open syllable, it makes a central sound. With an accent mark, or before a silent consonant as in (nez) /ne/, it makes a high sound. With a grave accent, or before a final consonant as in (mer) /mɛʁ/, it makes a lower sound. At the end of a word like (table) /tabl/, or inside (samedi) /sam.di/, the letter is not pronounced.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make the sound in (été) /e.te/ glide like the vowel in day. A diphthong has two vowel sounds that slide together. Keep your tongue completely still from start to finish. Also, do not pronounce the ending in (table) /tabl/ like the vowel in the English word sofa. Stop your voice right after the consonant sound.
